subject: QuantBridge — Security & support access confirmation and retention windows
messages:

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: support access model, break-glass & retention windows (post-demo)

Hi Elena / QuantBridge team,

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap from my side and three asks to keep momentum:

Key points we covered (short):
- RBAC baseline: customer-admin, security-admin (audit/forensics), support-readonly, support-operator (escalations).
- Break-glass: JIT escalation with time-limited scoped token (1-hour default), approval via customer-designated approver + audit trail.
- Logging & recording: session-level recording for escalations; all support sessions logged with request/response hashes (no PLAINTEXT by default).
- Retention: prompt/input retention default 30 days for hosted; logs/telemetry retained 13 months (can be scoped shorter for compliance).
- Data residency: option to pin workload to us-east (default) or eu-west for EU-resident workloads.

Asks / next steps: 
1) Can you confirm whether QuantBridge requires prompt storage beyond 30 days for any pilot teams? (yes/no + list)
2) Please confirm the break-glass approver(s) (name + email) who should receive immediate notifications.
3) If you want a SOC2 artifact packet, let me know the preferred format — we can share a scoped extract and the relevant control mappings.

Attachments: redwood-support-access-checklist.pdf (checklist), quantbridge-scoping-form.xlsx (we filled the infrastructure/residency sections you requested), data-retention-summary.md

Notes on security controls (brief):
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest with customer-specific KMS keys available on Dedicated/Private plans.
- Break-glass: token issuance is timeboxed, requires a two-step approval for requests > 90 minutes or access to labeled-PII resources.
- Least-privilege: support-operator sessions are scoped to transaction IDs/trace IDs rather than full dataset access — we can use temporary read-only tokens mapped to customer-admin policies.

If the QuantBridge security team prefers, Rishi is available to do a shorter follow-up call next week where we can walk through the checklist and the scoping form.

Thanks,

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround. Answers inline below.

> Can you confirm Redwood can send an outgoing webhook to PagerDuty (and include the approver email in the subject)?
Yes — we support outbound webhooks to PagerDuty and can include structured fields (approver email, request id, customer id). We also have an option to mirror notifications to an email distribution list (security@quantbridge.com) and create an audit event in your account stream.

> Can Redwood support per-workload retention overrides (90 days for pilot teams)?
Yes. Hosted allocations can be set per-workload. Default = 30 days (prompt inputs), retention options are 30/90/365 days for prompts, and logs/telemetry are configurable up to 13 months. For Dedicated/Private, you can enforce any retention by policy on your side. We'll surface a per-workload flag in the console and in the API.

> When support-operator is in a session, will they ever be able to view raw customer prompts or only redacted hashes?
By default, support-operator roles see redacted input with hashes and metadata. Full prompt visibility requires an explicit break-glass flow:
  - Request is raised by operator
  - Approver (your named approver) must click approve in the webhook / console (or approve via PagerDuty)
  - Token issued for N minutes (default 60) with session recording enabled
  - All actions logged and stored in immutable audit log (13 months by default).

SOC2 packet: I attached a scoped SOC2 controls extract (we provide a sanitized artifact for prospects). Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCExampleShare (see folder: QuantBridge-SOC2-Excerpt).

- Rishi to run a 30-min technical call to walk through the checklist + webhook demo (Tues 8/24 10:00am ET) — action: rishi to confirm calendar invite.
- QuantBridge to confirm break-glass approvers and pilot workloads that need 90-day retention by EOD Wed 8/25.
- Redwood to provide a short legal redline for the data retention addendum (we can use DocuSign once scopes are agreed).
